newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Dispute erupts over Jamaican cult movie classic.
newsitem.headline: Dispute erupts over Jamaican cult movie classic.

text.p: A proposed sequel to the Jamaican cult movie "The Harder They Come" could lead to a lawsuit between the two men who made the original film, reports said on Wednesday.

Reggae singer Jimmy Cliff's planned follow-up to the low-budget movie has not gone over well with Perry Henzell, who wrote and directed the original film in the early 1970s and owns the rights to the film.
Cliff, who played the role of an outlaw who became a folk hero by opposing the establishment, is planning to start filming "The Harder They Come II" in March, according to Jamaican press reports.
He plans to resurrect his character, Ivan, who died in the original movie's final scene.
But Henzell, who also has plans for his own sequel, said if Cliff goes ahead with his plans he will take legal action.
"He should not exploit what is not his," Henzell warned. "If he does I will be forced to sue him."

"The Harder They Come" was filmed on a shoestring budget but became enormously popular in Europe and the United States. It launched the career of Cliff, 52, providing him with a hit album, and Henzell, 60, a former writer of commercial jingles.
The film was responsible for popularising reggae music outside Jamaica and included the title song and other hits "Many Rivers to Cross" and "You Can Get It If You Really Want."

Cliff never reached the popularity enjoyed by reggae superstar Bob Marley, but has remained active and is popular in Europe and Africa. He has released more than 20 albums and won a Grammy award in 1985 for "Cliff Hanger," recorded with Kool and the Gang.
